seo.title: Blue Ventures Partnership - Oceans Alive Foundation
seo.description: In partnership with Blue Ventures Conservation, we strengthen fisheries monitoring and co-management capacity within the KAMAMKUKI Joint Co-Management Area across Kilifi and Mombasa Counties.

hero.eyebrow: In Partnership with Blue Ventures Conservation
hero.title: Strengthening Fisheries
hero.label: Monitoring Capacity
hero.text: A two-phase project to strengthen the fisheries monitoring and co-management capacity of five Beach Management Units within the KAMAMKUKI Joint Co-Management Area, promoting the use of reliable fisheries and ecological information to support informed, adaptive management of shared coastal resources.

theKamamkukiProject.heading: The KAMAMKUKI
theKamamkukiProject.label: Co-Management Area
theKamamkukiProject.text2: spans approximately 304 km² of coastal and marine waters within Kenya's territorial sea. It brings together the Kuruwitu, Kanamai and Mtwapa BMUs in Kilifi County and the Marina and Kidongo BMUs in Mombasa County.
theKamamkukiProject.text3: These institutions work alongside the Kenya Fisheries Service (KeFS) and the respective county governments to manage shared fisheries resources under the framework established by the Fisheries Management and Development Act No. 35 of 2016.
theKamamkukiProject.text4: "The project's approach is centred on building the capacity of BMUs and allied co-management institutions to implement fisheries regulations and management measures effectively and accountably."

projectPhases.heading: Building Capacity
projectPhases.label: Step by Step
projectPhases.text: The project responds to a set of interrelated pressures on the JCMA's fisheries and unfolds in two strategic phases from October 2024 to November 2026.
projectPhases.text2: Phase 1 focused on diagnosing and addressing governance and institutional capacity gaps across the five BMUs and establishing a fisheries catch-monitoring system at ten landing sites within the JCMA.
projectPhases.text3: Phase 2 builds on those foundations across four priority areas: strengthening BMU governance and compliance through a structured mentorship programme; promoting peer learning, knowledge exchange and collaboration among BMUs; improving the financial resilience of fisheries-dependent communities through Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs); and deepening fisheries and ecological monitoring to support evidence-based management decisions.

theChallenge.heading: Addressing Interrelated
theChallenge.label: Pressures
theChallenge.text: The project responds to a set of interrelated pressures on the JCMA's fisheries: destructive and illegal fishing practices, declining fish stocks, habitat degradation, weak enforcement, limited institutional capacity within co-management bodies, and the growing economic vulnerability of coastal communities whose livelihoods depend on increasingly stressed resources.

ourApproach.heading: A Community-Centred
ourApproach.label: Approach
ourApproach.text: Interventions span governance and institutional development, fisheries catch and ecological monitoring, compliance strengthening, financial resilience for fisheries-dependent households, and community food security.
